title: ulmus davidiana var. suberosa
intro: Ulmus davidiana var. suberosa, commonly known as Cork Elm or Maki, is a deciduous tree native to East Asia, characterized by its distinctive corky bark and broad leaves. This plant has been traditionally used to treat various health conditions, including fever, rheumatism, and digestive issues, due to its numerous health benefits. The therapeutic actions of Ulmus davidiana var. suberosa include anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which contribute to its healing effects. Its bioactive constituents include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and saponins, which are responsible for its medicinal properties and have been studied for their potential in treating various diseases.
